title: Census Night at the Farm
place: Farmhouse kitchen, Great House Farm, Llandough, Glamorgan

shots.direction: Date-and-place card. Early-morning establishing still of the farmhouse and yard, April 1881: stone house, limewashed walls, yard muck and puddles, a cart against the barn, smoke from the kitchen chimney. Slow push-in toward the kitchen door. Ambience only: hens, a distant dog, wind in bare hedges. About 8 seconds.

shots.direction: Wide still from the hill. Llandough fields and hedges run down to the Ely, with the marshes and the estuary far off under a grey sky. The view is inland, looking down. Slow lateral drift across the field pattern the surveyors had recently mapped. Ambience: skylark, wind. About 14 seconds.

shots.direction: Still of the rear wing of the farmhouse seen from the yard: older rubble masonry, a low doorway, a glimpse of a flagstone floor inside. No one is shown finding anything and no object is shown. Slow push toward the doorway. Ambience: dripping gutter. About 12 seconds.

captions.text: c.1880: 'Armour' is reported found under the floor of the rear wing of Great House. It is thought to be the medieval ironwork from Llandough now at the National Museum.

shots.direction: Kitchen door, inside looking out. The enumerator stands on the threshold in a dark frock coat with his leather document case, hat in hand, and speaks to Mary, who has opened the door. Medium shot on him.

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, formal and courteous (Welsh marked for native review)
lines.cy: Bore da, Mrs Williams. Wedi dod i nôl papur y cyfrifiad ydw i, yr un adewes i 'ma wthnos dwetha.
lines.en: Good morning, Mrs Williams. I've come to collect the census paper, the one I left here last week.
lines.es: Buen día, señora Williams. Vengo a buscar la planilla del censo, la que dejé acá la semana pasada.

shots.direction: Mary steps back to let him in. The kitchen behind her has an inglenook with a low fire, flagstones and a dresser of plates. Children are soft-focus background extras at the table. Medium close on Mary.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9 still, 1881 Welsh farmhouse kitchen, a Welsh woman in her late forties with strong cheekbones, grey-green eyes, a small mole on her left cheek, and dark brown hair with first grey in a bun, wearing a plain wool dress, a shawl and an apron, gesturing someone inside, an inglenook fireplace, flagstone floor and wooden dresser with plates behind her, blurred children at a table, oil lamp, invented faces, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, warm (Welsh marked for native review)
lines.cy: Dewch miwn, dewch miwn. Mae John wedi'i lenwi fe neithiwr wrth olau'r lamp. Pawb oedd dan y to 'ma neithiwr, fel y gofynnoch chi.
lines.en: Come in, come in. John filled it in last night by the lamplight. Everyone who was under this roof last night, as you asked.
lines.es: Pase, pase. John la llenó anoche a la luz del farol. Todos los que estaban bajo este techo anoche, como usted pidió.

shots.direction: John at the kitchen table, bareheaded, in shirtsleeves and waistcoat. He takes the folded schedule from behind a jug on the dresser and hands it over, reading down it as he does. Medium close on John.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9 still, 1881 Welsh farmhouse kitchen, a weathered Welsh farmer aged about 53 with a broad face, a grey-flecked beard and heavy hands, wearing shirtsleeves and a waistcoat, handing a folded printed form across a scrubbed wooden table to a man in a dark frock coat, inglenook and dresser behind, morning window light, invented faces, no legible text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, plain and steady (Welsh marked for native review)
lines.cy: Dyma fe. John Williams, penteulu, pum deg tri, ffermwr. Mary, y wraig. Wedyn y plant, yr hyna' gynta'. Popeth yn deidi, gobeitho.
lines.en: Here it is. John Williams, head, fifty-three, farmer. Mary, wife. Then the children, eldest first. All tidy, I hope.
lines.es: Acá está. John Williams, jefe de familia, cincuenta y tres, granjero. Mary, esposa. Después los chicos, del más grande al más chico. Todo prolijo, espero.

shots.direction: The enumerator sits at the end of the table, opens his enumeration book beside the schedule, dips his pen and looks up at John. Close-medium on him.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9 still, 1881 Welsh farmhouse kitchen, a pale clean-shaven man in his fifties with thin-rimmed spectacles and a dark frock coat, seated at a wooden table with a large open ledger and a folded printed form, holding a dip pen over an inkwell, looking up, leather document case on the table, soft window light, invented face, no legible text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, formal and courteous (Welsh marked for native review)
lines.cy: Diolch, Mr Williams. Fe gopïa i'r cyfan i'r llyfr fel mae e ar y papur, yr erwau a'r cwbwl. A'r tŷ... Llandough Home Farm. 'Na fe.
lines.en: Thank you, Mr Williams. I'll copy it all into the book as it stands on the paper, the acres and all. And the house... Llandough Home Farm. There.
lines.es: Gracias, señor Williams. Lo paso todo al libro tal como está en la planilla, los acres y todo. Y la casa... Llandough Home Farm. Listo.

shots.direction: Insert still: the pen moving across the ruled page of the enumeration book in copperplate, too close and soft to read. Mary's hand rests on the back of John's chair at the edge of frame. Slow push-in. Ambience: pen scratch, fire crackle. About 18 seconds.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9 close-up still, 1881, a dip pen writing in faded brown ink on a ruled ledger page with blurred illegible copperplate script, a wooden kitchen table, an inkwell, a woman's hand resting on a chair back at the edge of frame, warm firelight and window light, shallow depth of field, no legible text, no heraldry

captions.text: Census, 3 April 1881 (RG11/5288 p.2): John Williams, 53, 'Farmer of 170 [or 120] ac.', with his wife Mary and their children, at 'Llandough Home Farm', Llandough.
The page does not name Great House. On our case's reading, the census mixed up the Llandough farm with Great House Farm, so this is Great House Farm under another name.

shots.direction: The enumerator crosses the yard toward the lane with his case under his arm. Beyond the yard hedge are the orchard trees and, further off, the railway embankment. Slow pull-back. Ambience: hens, a distant train whistle. About 10 seconds.
